# Bonitz, *Index Aristotelicus* — sigla reference

Every abbreviation Bonitz defines before the index proper. Source is the
1870 Berlin original (archive.org `aristotelisopera05arisuoft`, leaves
261, 262, 264) at ~415 ppi. Provenance, reader comparison and the
measurements behind this are in `work/frontmatter/NOTES.md`.

Titles are given **in full**. Bonitz prints an em dash for a repeated
title; that is clear on the leaf and confusing here. The four rows whose
printed form differs are listed at the end.

---

## Work sigla (48 rows, 47 distinct)

A citation siglum is **work + book numeral**: `Ζιι` is `Ζι` + book ι,
`πκγ` is `π` + book κγ = 23. A vowel inside a siglum is either part of
the work siglum or a book numeral, never anything else.

⚠ A **bare book letter inherits the previous citation's work**.
`Ζιε13. 544a32. ζ1. 558b13` is HA book 6, not the work `ζ`. The Bekker
page adjudicates.

⚠ **Metaphysics book letters are names, not numerals** — Α α Β Γ … Μ Ν.

1866), tragedians **Nauck**, comedians **Meineke**, philosophers

## Where the leaf differs from the reference form

| siglum | printed | reference |
|---|---|---|
| `Αγδ` | —  ὕστερα | Ἀναλυτικὰ ὕστερα |
| `Η` | Ηθικὰ Νικομάχεια | Ἠθικὰ Νικομάχεια |
| `ημ` | —  μεγάλα | Ἠθικὰ μεγάλα |
| `ηε` | —  Εὐδήμεια | Ἠθικὰ Εὐδήμεια |

`Η` prints a bare eta — no smooth breathing — where every other capital
on the leaf carries its mark (`Ὕπνȣ`, `Ἀλέξανδρον`, `Ἑρμηνείας`).

## Conventions

- The kai abbreviation always carries a **grave**: `ϗ̀`, never bare.
  The corpus agrees 760 of 785.
- `ȣ` is a single sort. Never `ου`, never a bare `υ`.
- A circumflex over `ȣ` is U+0342 perispomeni, not U+0303.
- No stigma (ϛ) occurs anywhere in the front matter. Every sigma-family
  character here is a final sigma ς.
